newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products firmer apart from easier gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products firmer apart from easier gas oil.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were firmer on Tuesday, apart from gas oil.
Gasoline rose but traders said most interest was for lower octane grades, especially from Lebanon and Turkey. The arbitrage to the U.S. and NWE was seen shut.
"In the Med the situation is not so active as in the north," said one Italian trader. "The Med is not looking for Eurograde material and all Italian refiners are covered and balanced."
Naphtha ended up $3 at $219/$222 cif with traders still quoting fob at a wide $15 discount. Traders awaited the results of the 1997 Egyptian tender, expected this week.
Rumours circulated that it may be awarded at a premium between $6 and $6.50 over mean fob Med prices.
Gas oil retreated slightly in line with Nov IPE futures and business was thin but premiums were unchanged to firmer with very active demand for 0.2 per cent heating oil into Greece and Turkey.
One player who remains a buyer for Russian declined an offer of a cargo at cif quotes high +$2, a level also offered elsewhere for a Romanian cargo into the Med loading November 20-22.
Russian was also offered at cif quotes high +$4 basis Genoa.

High and low sulphur cracked fuel oil was a touch firmer with $110-111 fob Med heard talked on high sulphur paper. Traders said demand into Gibraltar for bunker spec was fair but matched by sufficient avails. The low sulphur cracked sector looked stronger after a late trade in NWE at $126.50 fob NWE.

Russian straight-run material was becoming increasingly scarce with M-40 very hard to source. Traders said notional prices were in the low $130s cif. High sulphur cargoes that are close to straight run were assessed a touch under $120 cif.
